A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CIDNet study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, checklists, and appendices. Renumbered tables and reorganized appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CASSI reconstruction simulations, real-data reconstructions, component ablations, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1–5 and Figures 6–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results, real-data reconstructions, ablations, and appendix analyses, with several numerical revisions in its intensity/chromaticity table.

M1.justification: The decomposition, intensity-guided sensing operator, HQS updates, hybrid attention, DNEM, and chromaticity training loss remain unchanged. The corrected mathematical signs reconcile the derivation with the existing solver; the added feedforward-network description does not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CAVE for training, the same 10 KAIST test scenes, and the real Ninja measurement. PAN/RGB-guided reconstruction examples and supplementary scene coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators remain DeSCI, GAP-Net, MST-L, DAUHST, SSR, PIDS, and In2SET; real-data and appendix comparator sets also match. New Table 1 compares ISTA, GAP, and HQS update formulas without adding an empirical baseline.

E3.justification: The training/test split, 300-epoch budget, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, patch sizes, dispersion settings, and PSNR/SSIM metrics are retained. PAN normalization and the parallel-attention channel split are newly disclosed details, without evidence that existing experimental protocols changed.

E4.justification: The component, attention, and intensity-mask ablations retain their configurations and results. Appendix reconstruction comparisons, HSI/chromaticity visualizations, and stagewise noise-map analyses are also retained; their relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 states in both versions that each task runs 10 instances with different random seeds. Uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2, now v2 Table 3, revises several CIDNet entries. CIDNet-9stg intensity PSNR changes from 61.26 to 65.86 on S4 and from 64.00 to 61.26 on S5; several chromaticity SSIMs change, including the five-stage average from 0.92 to 0.93. Main HSI scores remain unchanged. The reported 1.56 dB attention gain is correctly attributed to Base-2 instead of Base-1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Proposition A.1 and a proposed derivation of approximate PAN–intensity proportionality, substantially expanding the mathematical treatment of a central sensing assumption that v1 only asserted. Section 2.2 also corrects the negative data-fidelity terms in Equations 11–13 to positive terms. Existing illumination-invariance and HQS derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: illumination-invariant chromaticity decomposition, intensity-guided unfolding with hybrid attention and adaptive noise estimation, and superior reconstruction performance. Added terminology and supporting arguments do not change that scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains PAN as a relative intensity estimate under common illumination and motivates the approximation through normalized spectra and broadband response. It also explicitly contrasts spatially adaptive projection with conventional updates. The premeasured-intensity limitation and interpretations of the noise-map results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code/model-release promise with a stated code release and repository address. It additionally documents PAN normalization to [0,1] during training and inference, the feedforward network after spectral attention, and the half-channel split in the parallel-attention ablation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang and Ghanem's ISTA-Net citation and a focused comparison positioning its projection against ISTA, GAP, and HQS. The remaining cited works and broader research positioning are retained, with subsequent references renumbered.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify notation, component acronyms, and reconstruction comparisons. v2 adds acknowledgments, updates author footnotes, and consolidates Appendices A–D into Sections A.1–A.8 with an introductory roadmap. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the compact data-consistency comparison table, expands Figure 2's caption, adjusts ablation-table spacing, and relocates appendix figures. Existing experimental figures and benchmark-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency through the objective-sign corrections and clarifies numerical reporting, ablation attribution, and implementation details. It also supplies concrete code-access information. The empirical evidence remains essentially unchanged, and the new PAN-equivalence argument relies on an unquantified spatial-constancy approximation in Equation 38, limiting its theoretical benefit. Overall, the supported gains are useful but limited.
